author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: Harness provenance can only be declared as environment variables, so the model the primary harness publishes in its own session record is inexpressible: 900 of 900 explicit entries still record model null while effort resolves

Automatic identity is meant to record which model acted, so an agent never types an identity flag. Harness and reasoning effort are recorded correctly today. The model is not, and cannot be, because of how signal sources are declared rather than because of which keys are declared.

HarnessSignalDescriptor (src/core/shared/author.ts:58) can express exactly four kinds of evidence: environment_keys, model_environment_keys, session_environment_keys, provenance_environment_keys, plus argv_markers and client_names for identifying the harness itself. Every provenance dimension is therefore an environment variable by construction. analyzeAgentProvenanceDescriptorCoverage (src/sdk/provenance.ts:44) confirms the shape: coverage for a dimension is computed as whether any descriptor lists environment keys for it. A dimension a harness publishes through any other channel -- a file, a socket, a process attribute, a protocol handshake field -- is not merely undetected, it is inexpressible.

Measured at HEAD, build 2026.7.28, inside a real claude-code session:

  declared model sources for claude-code   ANTHROPIC_MODEL, CLAUDE_MODEL
  either variable present in the session    no
  variables the harness actually publishes  CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID,
                                            CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION,
                                            AI_AGENT (value carries harness and version)

A sandbox mutation recorded right now, with no author override:

  author            harness:claude-code
  author_source     detected
  agent_harness     claude-code
  agent_instance    4018c32541da6a6805d5bd7d
  agent_provenance  model: null, effort: xhigh from environment
  agent_model       null

Harness resolves. Effort resolves. Model is null, and the corpus agrees: across every history entry carrying explicit provenance, 848 record model null and 52 record model null with an effort observation. Zero observed models across 4,353 claude-code, 1,728 codex and 155 opencode entries.

The model is not missing from the machine. It is published, on disk, keyed by a variable pm already reads. CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is declared as this harness's session key and is set. The harness writes its own session record under a per-project directory named for the working directory, in a file named for that exact session id, and every assistant record in it carries the model identifier and the harness version. In the session that produced this item, 62 records carry model claude-opus-5 and the record header carries version 2.1.220. Joining a variable pm already reads to a file the harness already writes yields the missing dimension exactly.

This is why pm-0zcwz6, which closed correctly on what it delivered, did not change the outcome. It added environment, argv, and client model sources -- three more instances of the one channel the primary harness does not use for this dimension. Adding a fourth environment key cannot work, and the descriptor type offers nothing else to add.

What this item owns: a second class of signal source. A descriptor should be able to declare a resolver -- a named, bounded, side-effect-free probe that reads a location derived from already-detected signals -- alongside its environment keys, with the observation recording which source produced it, exactly as effort already records source environment today.

Constraints that are part of the requirement, not caveats. A probe reads local files that can contain arbitrary session content, so it must extract only the declared dimension value, never retain or copy surrounding content, be bounded in bytes and time, fail closed to null rather than erroring, and be disableable by configuration. It must never become a blocking dependency of a mutation. And the recorded provenance must distinguish a value observed from a probe from a value observed from the environment, so the corpus stays auditable.

Two adjacent observations that fall out of the same reading and belong to this item because they are the same channel question. AI_AGENT carries the harness version in the environment and AGENT_PROVENANCE_DIMENSIONS has no version dimension to receive it. CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION distinguishes a delegated sub-session from a root session, which is a role signal available in the environment right now.

Boundaries. pm-rbg1qo owns which dimensions are declared for which harnesses and the absent session-topic keys; that is a question about coverage within the existing channel and stays with it. pm-0zcwz6 and pm-itsjf0 are closed and correct about what they shipped. This item is only the claim that one channel is not enough, and that the missing dimension is reachable through a second one.

A harness signal descriptor can declare a non-environment resolver for any provenance dimension, alongside its environment keys; The claude-code descriptor resolves the model by joining its already-declared session key to the harness session record, and a live mutation records a non-null model with the source naming the probe; Provenance observations distinguish a probe-sourced value from an environment-sourced value, the way effort already records its source; A probe is bounded in bytes and time, extracts only the declared dimension, never retains surrounding content, fails closed to null, and never blocks or fails a mutation; Probing is disableable by configuration and its default is documented; A harness version dimension exists and is populated for at least one harness that publishes it; A negative control proves the descriptor coverage analysis reports a dimension as uncovered when neither an environment key nor a resolver can supply it

message: Filed from a live HEAD probe inside a real claude-code session. Neither declared model variable is set; CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is set and the harness session record it names carries model claude-opus-5 on 62 assistant records plus harness version 2.1.220. Sandbox mutation records harness and effort xhigh but agent_model null. Corpus: 848 plus 52 explicit provenance entries, zero observed models across 6,236 harness-attributed entries. Duplicate check: pm-0zcwz6 closed by adding more environment, argv and client sources, which is the same channel; pm-itsjf0 closed on dimension extensibility; pm-rbg1qo owns per-harness dimension coverage; none owns the claim that the descriptor vocabulary admits only one channel.

value.text:
Live re-measure 2026-07-28 on this repository's own tracker, taken from the most recent entry of a real mutation stream rather than from a synthetic probe. The recorded provenance is:

  author           harness:claude-code
  author_source    detected
  agent_harness    claude-code
  agent_instance   present, a 24-character digest
  agent_provenance model null, effort {value: xhigh, source: environment}

So three of the four dimensions the maintainer directive asks for are live and correct - harness, instance, and thinking level - and are obtained with no PM_AUTHOR and no --author, which is the mandate. The two that remain absent are exactly the two this item and pm-itsjf0 own: model stays null because the harness publishes no model key for any resolver to read, and session topic and role are carried by zero entries because no environment signal exists to detect them. Nothing about the measurement has changed since it was filed; recorded here so the claim rests on a current reading rather than a recalled one.

value.text:
Live provenance re-measure 2026-07-30, from a create entry written by this session. The entry carries: author harness:claude-code, author_source detected, agent_harness claude-code, agent_instance a 24-hex handle, and agent_provenance with effort resolved as value xhigh source environment. It carries model null.

So the split this item names is stable and unchanged: the thinking level resolves from the environment and the model does not, because the harness publishes no model key of any kind. There is still no field anywhere on the entry for session topic or session role, so the maintainer request for an identity that reads like a model plus a thinking level plus a session role is currently one third delivered, one third blocked on a non-environment channel, and one third without a schema slot at all.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Post-fix corpus measurement 2026-07-31, and a conformance check against the closed pm-0zcwz6.

pm-0zcwz6 closed on 2026-07-27 with resolution 'Added working environment, argv, and client model sources plus model capture analysis that distinguishes observed, unavailable, legacy-missing, and inert descriptors' and actual_result 'Installed CLI history persisted gpt-5.6-sol with override source'. The channels shipped and the analysis shipped. The practical condition its own title names has not changed.

Counted over all 44,408 history entries in this tracker: 2,814 entries carry a model key and every one is an explicit null. Zero observed models corpus-wide, including every entry written after the 2026-07-27 close. Across 4,772 claude-code entries and 3,223 codex entries there is not one observed model. summarizeAgentModelProvenance's inert predicate - explicit sample present and observed zero - is therefore true for all three harnesses present in the corpus.

The evidence pm-0zcwz6 closed on is worth naming precisely, because it is the one source that cannot generalize: the persisted gpt-5.6-sol value came from the override source, meaning PM_AGENT_MODEL was set. Overrides require an agent or operator to type an identity value, which is exactly what the project's standing mandate forbids and exactly what this item exists to avoid. So the close verified that a manual channel works, while the automatic channels this item is about remain unobserved on every real entry.

Live probe, same session, 2026-07-31, confirms the mechanism is unchanged at HEAD: under Claude Code with CLAUDECODE set, a CLI-written entry records author harness:claude-code, author_source detected, agent_provenance {model: null, effort: {value: xhigh, source: environment}}. The effort dimension resolves from CLAUDE_EFFORT, which the harness does export. Neither ANTHROPIC_MODEL nor CLAUDE_MODEL is present in the environment, so the model dimension resolves to nothing and is written as an explicit null. The asymmetry inside a single entry is the sharpest statement of this item: one dimension of the same schema, from the same harness, in the same process, is observed, and the other is structurally unobservable because the harness does not publish it to the environment.

That asymmetry also argues for the scope this item should take. Since effort proves the environment channel works when a harness cooperates, and model proves it fails when a harness does not, the remedy cannot be more environment keys. It has to be a channel that does not depend on harness cooperation. pm-1zhfls and pm-9wbiye were filed against the recording mechanism this week and both bear on the design.

value.text: Still live at 2026.8.2, measured 2026-08-02 from a raw sandbox history entry written by this session (op history_compact_baseline): author 'harness:claude-code', author_source 'detected', agent_harness 'claude-code', agent_instance present, and agent_provenance = {model: null, effort: {value: 'xhigh', source: 'environment'}, role: null, topic: null}. So harness, instance and effort all resolve while model, role and topic remain null on an entry written by a harness that publishes its model in its own session record. Identity is correctly automatic - no PM_AUTHOR was set and no --author was passed - which is exactly why the missing model is the whole remaining gap: an agent pays nothing to record identity and still cannot record WHICH model acted. The maintainer directive restated this session is that provenance should resolve to the granularity of 'Opus 5 xhigh' plus session topic and role, so effort alone is one of four fields.
